title: Japanese F-2 Fighter Appears With New Large Stealth Cruise Missile Under Its Wings
summary: The previously unseen missile could be the air-launched Type 25, dramatically expanding the F-2’s standoff strike reach. The post Japanese F-2 Fighter Appears With New Large Stealth Cruise Missile Under Its Wings appeared first on TWZ .
detail: A Japanese F-2 fighter jet was recently observed carrying a new, large, and stealthy cruise missile, which is believed to be the air-launched Type 25. This development is significant because it dramatically expands the F-2’s standoff strike capabilities, allowing it to engage targets from a much greater distance without entering heavily defended airspace. This enhancement is crucial for Japan's evolving defense strategy, which increasingly emphasizes counter-strike capabilities to deter potential adversaries. The introduction of a stealthy missile suggests an intent to penetrate sophisticated air defense systems. This move aligns with Japan's broader efforts to bolster its military strength and adapt to a more challenging regional security environment, particularly concerning geopolitical tensions with China and North Korea, by providing its forces with more potent and flexible offensive options.

title: Japan Has Officially Joined The Tomahawk Cruise Missile Club
summary: Japan has fired its first Tomahawk from one of its destroyers, ushering in a new era of long-range cruise missile capability. The post Japan Has Officially Joined The Tomahawk Cruise Missile Club appeared first on TWZ .
detail: Japan has officially joined the 'Tomahawk Cruise Missile Club' by successfully test-firing one of these long-range missiles from a destroyer. This marks a pivotal moment in Japan's defense policy, signifying its acquisition and operationalization of a proven, precision-strike weapon capable of hitting land targets from naval platforms. The Tomahawk provides Japan with a substantial new capability for deterrence and response, allowing it to project power over significant distances. This acquisition is part of Japan's strategic shift to enhance its 'counter-strike capabilities,' a policy change driven by increasing regional security concerns, particularly from China and North Korea. While domestically controversial, the government views these missiles as essential for national security, complementing other efforts to modernize its military and ensure a credible defense posture in the Indo-Pacific.

title: US Navy Awards Historic $76.6B Contract for 9 Block VI Virginia SSNs and 5 Columbia SSBNs
summary: In its largest-ever submarine deal, the US Navy awards $76.6B to GDEB and HII for 9 Block VI Virginia-class attack subs and 5 Columbia-class SSBNs. U.S Navy press release On July, 29 2026, the Department of War expanded its undersea warfighting capabilities by awarding a five-ship contract modification to General …
detail: The US Navy has awarded a historic $76.6 billion contract to General Dynamics Electric Boat and Huntington Ingalls Industries for the construction of nine Block VI Virginia-class attack submarines (SSNs) and five Columbia-class ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs). This massive investment is critical for maintaining the US Navy's undersea dominance and ensuring the continuity of its strategic nuclear deterrent. Virginia-class SSNs are versatile, multi-mission platforms vital for intelligence gathering, special operations, and anti-submarine warfare. The Columbia-class SSBNs are the future backbone of the sea-based leg of the nuclear triad, replacing the aging Ohio-class and guaranteeing continuous nuclear deterrence. This contract underscores the immense cost and long lead times associated with advanced submarine construction, while also securing the health of the US submarine industrial base and workforce amidst growing global competition in the undersea domain.

detail: British defense company Babcock is actively seeking to expand its naval opportunities in the Asia-Pacific market, building on its recent success in licensing the Arrowhead 140 frigate design to Indonesia. The company is now targeting further partnerships in countries like New Zealand. This initiative reflects a broader trend of international defense firms increasing their presence in the Asia-Pacific, a region undergoing significant naval modernization and expansion due to geopolitical tensions and economic growth. Babcock's strategy of licensing designs allows nations to build ships domestically, fostering local industry and technology transfer, which is often preferred over direct imports. This approach enables regional navies to acquire modern capabilities, such as the adaptable and cost-effective Arrowhead 140 frigates, thereby enhancing their maritime security and defense postures in a strategically vital area.

title: SpaceX wins $1.6B to launch Space Force ‘sensing and targeting’ sats
summary: The SpaceX task order is the first to be awarded since the Space Force’s July 17 massive $11.4 billion plus-up to the NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 contract vehicle ceiling.
detail: SpaceX has secured a $1.6 billion task order from the US Space Force to launch 'sensing and targeting' satellites. This is the first major award under the recently expanded $11.4 billion National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 3 Lane 1 contract vehicle. This contract highlights the US Space Force's commitment to enhancing its space-based intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance (ISR), and targeting capabilities. These satellites are crucial for providing real-time data to military operations on Earth, improving situational awareness, and enabling precision strikes in modern warfare. For SpaceX, this award solidifies its position as a primary launch provider for critical national security missions, leveraging its cost-effective and high-cadence launch capabilities. This move also reflects a broader strategy to diversify launch providers and integrate commercial innovation into national security space programs.
